## Files changed
- `src/auth/token.mjs` adds the env fallback. I also added a second header comment line describing the order. The signature (`options = {}`) and return type (string) are unchanged.
- `src/auth/token.test.mjs` now saves and restores `process.env.API_TOKEN` around every test (deleting it if it was originally unset). No existing test asserted the absence of an env fallback, so none had to be rewritten. The original "returns the explicit token" test is kept. I added tests for:
  - (a) no argument plus `API_TOKEN` set uses the env value
  - (b) an explicit argument plus `API_TOKEN` set uses the argument
  - (c) no argument plus `API_TOKEN` unset throws, as before
  - an empty-string argument falls back to the env value
  - an empty-string `API_TOKEN` is treated as unset and throws
- `src/auth/PRECEDENT.md` has the §explicit-token block rewritten in place (text below).

## Final implementation
```js
// Resolves the API token for a client instance.
// Order: an explicit `options.token`, then `process.env.API_TOKEN`. Empty strings count as absent.

export function resolveToken(options = {}) {
  if (typeof options.token === "string" && options.token.length > 0) {
    return options.token;
  }
  const envToken = process.env.API_TOKEN;
  if (typeof envToken === "string" && envToken.length > 0) {
    return envToken;
  }
  throw new Error("resolveToken: pass { token } explicitly");
}
```

## New PRECEDENT.md text
The file had no existing pattern for superseded decisions. I kept the `§explicit-token` anchor and added `Amended` and `History` fields beside the existing `Since`, `Decision`, `Forbidden` and `Evidence` fields.
```md
### §explicit-token — an explicit token wins; `API_TOKEN` is the only fallback
- Since: 2026-09-20
- Amended: 2026-10-23 — the maintainer overrode the original decision (no environment fallback). The override was a
  maintainer decision; no rationale was given.
- Decision: `resolveToken` returns `options.token` if it is a non-empty string, otherwise `process.env.API_TOKEN` if it
  is a non-empty string, otherwise throws. An explicit token always wins over the environment variable.
- Forbidden: falling back to any environment variable other than `API_TOKEN`, or to a dotfile.
- Evidence: `token.test.mjs`
- History: until 2026-10-23 the decision was "`resolveToken` returns `options.token` or throws. It never reads
  environment variables or files", forbidding any `process.env` fallback. Its reason was: tests and the dev server share
  one process environment; an environment fallback let a test run hit the API with a developer's production token
  (incident 2026-09-19). Passing it explicitly kept the token's origin visible at the call site. That reason is kept
  here as history only; it was not the basis for the override and the override did not address it.
```

## Test command and result
Command: `npm test` (which runs `node --test`). I also ran `API_TOKEN=outer-value npm test` to confirm the tests don't depend on the ambient environment.
```
ℹ tests 8
ℹ pass 8
ℹ fail 0
ℹ cancelled 0
ℹ skipped 0
```
There were no failures, including in the unrelated `tab-keys` tests.

## Judgment calls
- **Empty strings:** the old code treated an empty `token` like a missing one, because both reached the throw. I kept that. An empty argument counts as "no token passed" and falls through to `API_TOKEN`. An empty `API_TOKEN` counts as unset, so the function throws. A more conservative alternative is to throw when `token: ""` is passed explicitly, without checking the env. I didn't choose it because it would change how empty arguments are treated.
- **No-token behavior:** it still throws. I left the error message as `resolveToken: pass { token } explicitly`, because you said not to invent new behavior. It is now slightly incomplete, since setting `API_TOKEN` also works. You may want to reword it, for example to "pass { token } or set API_TOKEN". The tests match only the `resolveToken:` prefix, so rewording won't break them.
- **Scope of the override:** I treated the override as covering only `API_TOKEN`. The record still forbids other env variable names and dotfiles. If the maintainer meant to lift the whole prohibition, that line needs widening.
- **Original rationale:** the incident risk behind the old rule (a test run using a developer's production token) is no longer guarded by the code. I recorded the rationale as history only and noted that the override didn't address it. I did not invent a new rationale.
- **Other docs:** the other four `PRECEDENT.md` files, `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md` don't mention the no-env-fallback rule, so I left them alone. The only other `env` hit in the repo is `CONTEXT_RAIL_LOG` in `.claude/hooks/precedent-context.py`, which is unrelated. `resolveToken` has no callers other than its test.
- **Hook confirmation:** a `PostToolUse` hook said an override counts only when the brief reports that the user named the decision and said to override it. I treated your brief as meeting that, because it names §explicit-token and says the maintainer overrode it on 2026-10-23.
